note: Laboratory notes written by hand, in the registers a notebook actually uses. Not generated from a template, and not written by a person doing the experiment either, so it is a register check and not a corpus. The quantity kinds are QUDT names and the units are QUDT unit names, so the grader scores these the same way it scores the synthetic set.

notes.text: Ran the column again after lunch. Back pressure sat at 118 bar the whole time, which is higher than Tuesday but still inside spec.
Weighed out the standard: 24.6 mg. Dissolved in the usual buffer, no issues.
Oven never reached setpoint. Logged 412 K at the thermocouple after forty minutes and I gave up waiting.
Sample 7b. Conductivity 3.4 mS/cm, measured twice, second reading agreed to the first decimal.
NB: the flow meter is reading low again. 0.85 mL/min on the display against 1.0 set. Service ticket raised.
Film thickness came out at 240 nm by ellipsometry. Thinner than the last batch, probably the spin speed.
Left the reaction stirring overnight, about 16 h in total, then quenched.
Titration endpoint at 12.35 mL. Repeat tomorrow with the fresh titrant, this bottle is three months old.
Cell voltage held at 1.23 V for the duration. No drift worth noting.
Density measured 1.045 g/cm3 at room temperature. Matches the supplier sheet within rounding.
Second attempt. Applied 45 N and the joint held, which it did not at 40 N yesterday.
pH meter calibrated first thing. Sample read 7.4, buffer read 7.0 as expected.
notes.skip: pH is not a QUDT quantity kind with a unit enumeration, so this one is kept as a case the corpus cannot score and must not be counted. The expected block names Volume and is an authoring error left in place, because the loader refuses a skip marker on a note that resolves and this one has to keep failing to resolve for that check to mean anything.

notes.text: Heating rate set to 5 K/min for the whole ramp. Trace looks clean.
Grabbed a quick reading before packing up: 96.2 kPa on the barometer.
Yield 0.82 g from the second crop. Combined with the first that is most of the theoretical.
Wavelength scan: peak at 532 nm, sharp, no shoulder this time.
Ambient was 21 degC and 44 percent humidity when I started. Noting it because the last run drifted.
Ran at 12000 rpm for ten minutes. Pellet was firm.
notes.skip: AngularVelocity admits only radian per second, hour and minute, so there is no identifier for rpm to resolve to and no arm could emit the expected unit. Checked before re-annotating: RotationalFrequency admits per_minute, but so does RotationalVelocity, and both are in the catalogue. Re-annotating to either would swap a note no model can answer for one where two answers are defensible and one is marked wrong, so it stays out.

notes.text: Resistance across the contacts 4.7 ohm. Same as before the anneal, so the anneal did nothing.
Energy input logged as 2.4 kJ over the pulse train. Detector saturated near the end so treat with care.
